findings.failure_mode: Missing file, permission denied, or unreadable path causes thread panic instead of returning a typed error
findings.fix: Change return type to Result<Vec<Record>, std::io::Error> and use fs::read_to_string(path)? or explicit match with typed error

findings.problem: as u16 is a lossy width-reducing cast from u32 to u16
findings.failure_mode: Values > 65535 silently truncate to u16 range, producing incorrect data without any error signal
findings.fix: Use u16::try_from(parsed_u32)? to detect overflow and return a typed conversion error

findings.failure_mode: Malformed CSV field (non-digit characters) causes panic instead of returning a ParseError
findings.fix: Use .parse::<u32>().map_err(|e| ...)? to propagate parse failures as typed errors

findings.problem: parts[0] uses unchecked indexing on Vec<String>
findings.failure_mode: Empty or malformed line causes panic via out-of-bounds index access
findings.fix: Use parts.get(0).ok_or(ErrorKind::InvalidInput) or split_once(',') and match on both results

findings.problem: parts[1] uses unchecked indexing on Vec<String>
findings.failure_mode: Line with only one comma-separated field causes panic via out-of-bounds index access
findings.fix: Use parts.get(1).ok_or(ErrorKind::InvalidInput) or split_once(',') and match on both results

findings.problem: split(',') + collect() + indexing instead of split_once(',') for two-field extraction
findings.failure_mode: Unnecessary heap allocation of Vec<String> per line, plus vulnerability to extra comma-separated fields that are silently ignored
findings.fix: Use line.split_once(',') and match on (left, right) to extract exactly two fields without intermediate Vec allocation

findings.problem: println!("loaded {}", parts[0]) in library code is an unrequested side effect
findings.failure_mode: Leaked logging in a library function; caller cannot suppress output without global config; stdout pollution
findings.fix: Remove println! entirely. If caller needs progress, accept a callback or return intermediate metadata

findings.problem: load_sessions mixes I/O (fs::read_to_string, println) with data parsing in a single function
findings.failure_mode: Cannot unit-test the parsing logic in isolation from filesystem; any test requires a real file on disk
findings.fix: Split into parse_record(line: &str) -> Result<Record, ParseError> (pure core) and load_sessions(path: &str) -> Result<Vec<Record>, IoError> (shell that calls parse_record)

findings.problem: Function signature returns Vec<Record> but all operations inside are fallible (I/O, parse, indexing, cast)
findings.failure_mode: Caller has no way to distinguish success from partial failure; no error information is communicated
findings.fix: Change signature to load_sessions(path: &str) -> Result<Vec<Record>, SessionLoadError> where SessionLoadError is a domain enum covering Io, Parse, and InvalidRecord variants

residual_risk: Static review only; no commands run. All operations in load_sessions are unguarded fallible paths (I/O, parsing, unchecked indexing, lossy cast). Every code path from malformed input to missing file will panic. The entire function is untestable without filesystem fixtures.
